plotSections.title: Planning the Next Destination
bullets: The party's immediate goal is to track down the lich and investigate leads connected to Grixto and Galixtar. They consider returning to Langdale for information, investigating the lich's former hideout in The Reach, and eventually visiting the Dragon Rider training grounds.

The Reach is accessible by the party's boat, by a captain who regularly travels between realms, or through the gatehouse using its keystones. Walker's Gate spell cannot transport the boat because its maximum diameter is 20 feet.
The party has sufficient food and water aboard the boat and can potentially resupply at a centrally located port city in The Reach.

plotSections.title: The Party's Crew and Elrus
bullets: The party confirms that their four surviving-and-revived crew members are Abel, Garrett, Bill, and Fritz. Abel is the helmsman and Garrett is the gunner; the exact roles of Bill and Fritz remain unclear, although one is believed to be a greenhorn.
Walker has an obligation to take Elrus somewhere because he previously promised the very old man a place to stay. Walker plans to bring Elrus with him when investigating The Reach.

plotSections.title: Grixto, Galixtar, and the Dragon Rider Training Grounds
bullets: The party has a lead suggesting Grixto and Galixtar were near caves associated with the Dragon Rider training grounds. Walker's previous vision prompted interest in investigating the area.

The caves and Walker's former roost in The Reach are believed to have been uninhabited for a long time, making it uncertain whether Grixto remains there. Walker nevertheless wants to exhaust the lead.

The training grounds are roughly a couple of days' flight from Walker's former residence in The Reach. From the area near the Whispering Abyss, the training grounds are approximately five days of flight away, near the Lost Isles and mountains between three islands.

Sylan prefers any investigation to remain a scouting mission so that a confrontation with Grixto occurs only when the entire party can respond. Walker considers traveling with Elrus and Araden, although he recognizes the danger of encountering Grixto.
Walker also wants to visit The Reach to recharge his gems.

plotSections.title: Al Kurin
bullets: Grixto had been collecting Al Kurin from other trainees at the Dragon Rider training grounds, including juvenile dragons.
An Al Kurin is a vessel capable of containing and transporting a dragon's soul, so the collected vessels do not necessarily have to remain at the training grounds.
The proximity of the training grounds to Walker's former residence makes it difficult to explain how Grixto could have remained there unnoticed for an extended period.

plotSections.title: The Lich and Its Phylactery
bullets: The party has learned more about the lich but remains uncertain about his current location and the identity of his phylactery.

The party believes the phylactery is a mundane object that the lich keeps on his person. His repeated association with small chess-like or war-game pieces leads Sylan to speculate that a chess set or one of its pieces could be the phylactery.
The party's lore establishes that a phylactery is a vessel containing a lich's soul, although they do not know the precise mechanics by which the lich returns after bodily destruction.

plotSections.title: Walker's Scouting Expedition
bullets: Walker plans to travel to The Reach with Elrus and Araden to investigate the Dragon Rider training grounds and search for information about Grixto and Galixtar.
The group intends to remain small and mobile and to retreat immediately if they encounter serious danger rather than initiating a confrontation.

Walker takes the party's sending stone so he can communicate with the others once per day using a message of up to 25 words. The party is uncertain how its recharge interacts with The Reach's unusual flow of time.

Walker initially intends to retain his keystone during the expedition despite Sylan suggesting that he leave it with the party for safety. The party also worries that storing multiple keystones together in a Bag of Holding could create an especially valuable target.

Plymouth Gawater ultimately joins Walker, Elrus, Araden, and Glimmen after consulting Juten Prime. Plymouth's investigation is intended to uncover information about the Dragon Riders, the keystones, and Grixto and Galixtar.

plotSections.title: Time Between Realms
bullets: The party estimates that traveling from their current location to Langdale takes roughly five to seven days by boat.

Time flows differently in The Reach, with the party discussing an approximate ratio of one day in their current realm to seven days in The Reach. Walker can therefore spend considerably longer in The Reach while only a relatively short period passes for the rest of the party.
The party plans to travel toward Langdale while Walker's group conducts its investigation and expects the unusual time difference to affect when they reconnect.

plotSections.title: Keystone and Gatehouse Mechanics
bullets: Plymouth explains that keystones must be properly seated and calibrated by the gatehouse's Doorman before a gate can be safely activated. Gerk, as the current Doorman, is responsible for helping orient and calibrate the stones.

A keystone used to open a gate must remain at the originating gatehouse while the gate is open. It can only be removed after the gate is closed, and tampering with a keystone during activation can cause dangerous malfunctions, as demonstrated by the earlier Gilbrick incident.
The gate functions as a connection between locations rather than allowing the keystone itself to travel through the gate.
Walker immediately activates the Reach gate despite Plymouth's explanation and travels through it with Glimmen, Elrus, and Araden. Plymouth then joins the expedition.

With Plymouth gone, the remaining party will rely on Gerk to operate the keystones and gates. Juten Prime safeguards the two unclaimed keystones while the party takes responsibility for the keystones they have claimed.

plotSections.title: The Ruined Archives and Keystone Research
bullets: The mountain's former libraries and archives are largely destroyed. Evidence suggests both deliberate raiding and natural deterioration, with paper materials mostly gone and stone, slate, and tile records broken or removed.
Only roughly the upper third of the mountain has been explored, leaving substantial portions of the site unexamined.
Sylan theorizes that information in the surviving archives may explain how Grixto learned to use the keystones.
Dana finds little immediately useful research remaining but wants to discuss Plymouth's discoveries about the gatehouse and its history when he returns.
Juten Prime agrees to safeguard the two remaining keystones and continue investigating the site while Plymouth pursues the Dragon Rider lead.

plotSections.title: Gerk Experiments with the Doorman Ability
bullets: After Walker's departure, Gerk begins experimenting with his new Doorman ability, which allows him to open door-like portals by concentrating on destinations.

His first experiments open onto radically different environments, including a murky body of water that sends swamp-smelling water through the opening and a barren, rocky landscape with geysers, intense heat, steam, and sulfurous air.
The portals manifest as tangible-looking doors that are actually openings or reflections of another location. Opening or closing one takes an action in combat.
Gerk and Sylan plan to continue practicing the ability during the voyage, initially attempting to reach familiar locations such as Gerk's home.

plotSections.title: The Moving Ship Doorway
bullets: Gerk attempts to open a door to his house while standing at the rear of the moving ship. Sylan uses Beacon of Hope to assist with the required Wisdom saving throws, and both avoid losing sanity.

The open doorway causes the ship and surrounding reality to stretch in a rubber-band-like distortion while the doorway remains fixed in place. The ship itself continues moving rather than physically slowing down.
The doorway exerts a powerful pull on Gerk. He makes a Strength saving throw and rolls 31, allowing him to hold onto it despite the force.

Mahali appears through the doorway from his kitchen and pulls Gerk through to safety. Passing through the doorway feels like moving through thick smoke or water, and the doorway remains open after Gerk passes through.

When the ship reverses course, the distortion reverses with it and eventually brings the ship back into alignment with the doorway. The incident demonstrates that using the ability from a moving vessel can dangerously distort space and reality.

plotSections.title: Closing the Door
bullets: The party decides to close the unstable doorway after preparing ropes and other precautions and evacuating Mahali's stronghold as a safety measure.

Gerk steps through the doorway and experiences another temporal or dimensional transition before closing it. The closure produces a quiet snap, followed by blinding light tracing the stretched path between the ship's previous and current positions.
Gerk rolls a 5 on a d10 for the door's effect. The DM describes the result as roughly midway on the relevant chart and pauses to determine the unexpected consequences.
The party braces for the possibility of being displaced or otherwise harmed, with Dana prepared to use Feather Fall if necessary.

plotSections.title: The Magical Discharge
bullets: Closing Gerk's doorway triggers a powerful magical discharge that causes reality around the ship to snap back into cohesion.
Gerk fails a Wisdom save and becomes confused and unable to act normally, while Sylan succeeds and remains functional.
Everyone aboard appears to blink out of existence or become invisible to the others. The party can still physically interact, but normal sight and sound between individuals are disrupted.

Dana and Sylan recognize the magical sensation as similar to what they experienced in the presence of deities and realize that their spells have become greatly empowered. All expended spell slots are restored.
A giant, closed, shining spectral door appears near where Gerk had been standing. Its appearance strongly resembles Gerk's door when his shield is in door form.
A thin golden, semi-fluorescent line remains embedded through the ship along the path of the magical discharge, resembling a lightning strike without causing physical damage.

plotSections.title: The Party's Separation
bullets: The party remains unable to see one another, recalling a similar separation that occurred in La-rel. Normal sounds do not reliably travel between the separated individuals.

Physical interaction remains possible despite the invisibility. Ciri can make contact with Sylan, Sylan can touch Gerk, and vibrations through the ship can be detected even when the associated sounds cannot.
Gerk remains confused and largely unable to communicate, making him especially difficult to locate and assist.

plotSections.title: The Spectral Door and Gerk
bullets: The spectral door continues hovering near Gerk, who is invisible and unable to move normally.
Sylan discovers Gerk by physically walking into him and attempts to support and reposition him. Gerk eventually allows himself to fall, and Sylan catches and lowers him.
Sylan turns Gerk toward the spectral door and attempts to determine whether the door or the forces around it are responsible for Gerk's condition.

plotSections.title: Attempts to Communicate and Restore Visibility
bullets: Sylan uses coins arranged on the deck to create visible messages for the unseen party members, eventually indicating Gerk's name and location.
Ord considers using powder or dust to reveal invisible people but instead uses his dragon vessel to pour olive oil over himself.
The oil experiment partially succeeds: although Ord remains invisible, the oil forms a faint, visible, largely silent silhouette outlining the portions of his body it covers.

Dana summons a large constrictor snake from her serpentine bracers and keeps it near her heel, giving her another visible marker for tracking her position. The DM establishes that the command can produce two constrictor snakes, though whether they can be released individually remains unresolved.

bullets: While the party deals with the magical aftermath, Walker describes The Reach as being in autumn, with crisp weather around 60 degrees and changing fall colors.

The Reach has a flying-themed culture, including the National Flying League, a flying sport jokingly compared to Quidditch, floating jack-o'-lanterns, and seasonal apple cider sold by a familiar turtle-like vendor.

chronologicalEventsDeduped: The party discusses whether to return to Langdale or investigate the lich's former hideout in The Reach, ultimately deciding to pursue the lead in The Reach before returning to Nyx or Langdale.
Sylan proposes searching the lich's former cave in The Reach for clues, including information that might help locate Grixto or his phylactery.

The party discusses traveling to The Reach by boat or using a captain who regularly travels between realms, with speed being the primary consideration. They confirm the ship has sufficient food and water and can resupply at a port city.

The crew is identified as Abel, Garrett, Bill, and Fritz. Dana identifies Garrett as the gunner and Abel as the helmsman, while the exact roles of Bill and Fritz remain uncertain. Dana also recalls that previously dead crew members were revived.
Walker asks whether his Gate can transport the party's boat. The DM explains that Gate creates a 5-to-20-foot-diameter opening, so the boat cannot pass unless it fits within the 20-foot limit.
Walker remembers that he still needs to fulfill his promise to provide Elrus with a place to stay and asks whether Elrus would accompany him to The Reach or remain in Midgard.
The party discusses hunting Grixto and Galixtar in The Reach based on a previous vision of them near caves and the Dragon Rider training grounds.

Walker explains that the old roost in The Reach appears largely abandoned and that he has already searched it without finding anything. The party considers sending Walker and a companion to scout while the others gather information elsewhere.

Sylan asks Elrus about the Al Kurin from the vision. Elrus explains that Grixto had been collecting these dragon-soul vessels from trainees, including juvenile dragons, and that they could be used to transport dragon souls.

The party determines that the Dragon Rider training grounds are only a few days' flight from Walker's former location near the Lost Isles. Because the area is close to Walker's former residence and Grixto could have moved the Al Kurin, they consider it unlikely that Grixto is still hiding there unless the area is investigated directly.

Sylan and Walker discuss their lack of progress locating the lich and his phylactery. They review their knowledge that a phylactery contains the lich's soul and conclude that Grixto's is believed to be a mundane object he keeps on his person.
The party identifies Grixto's recurring chess-like or war-game pieces as a possible clue to the mundane object that serves as his phylactery.
Walker and Sylan agree that The Reach is worth investigating before abandoning the lead, but Walker should avoid engaging Grixto unless necessary.
Walker explains that he wants to keep Araden and Elrus's capabilities hidden from Grixto so they can serve as concealed assets or a secret weapon during a future decisive confrontation.
Walker plans to travel to The Reach with Elrus and Araden, with Glimmen accompanying them, while the rest of the party continues toward Langdale and gathers information.
Walker proposes traveling to The Reach partly to recharge his gems. The party agrees that his trip should be a scouting mission rather than an attempt to fight the lich.

Walker takes the party's sending stone so he can report his findings. The stone allows one 25-word message per day, though the party discusses uncertainty about how its recharge interacts with The Reach's altered time flow.

The party establishes that Langdale is roughly a week away and that The Reach has a significant time differential, with approximately seven days passing in The Reach for every day outside it. Walker intends to exploit the extra apparent time for his activities.
Walker recalls that the arch previously deposited the party near the Whispering Abyss and that the Dragon Rider training grounds are roughly five days of flight from there.

Walker asks Plymouth Gawater how to use his keystone to travel to The Reach. Plymouth explains that Gerk, as the Doorman, must calibrate the gatehouse and correctly seat the keystone before it can safely be used.

Plymouth explains that an activated gate cannot simply be closed from the far side and that the keystone must remain seated in the originating gatehouse until the gate is shut. Improperly handling an activating keystone can cause malfunctions.
Walker activates the gate to The Reach and departs with Glimmen, Elrus, and Araden to investigate the Dragon Rider training grounds and the origins of Grixto and Galixtar.
Walker briefly returns to retrieve the sending stone before leaving through the gate.
Walker invites Plymouth Gawater to accompany the expedition. Plymouth consults Juten Prime, receives approval, prepares for travel, and joins Walker's group.
Plymouth warns the remaining party that Gerk will be responsible for operating the keystones while Plymouth is away.

Sylan asks Juten Prime to safeguard the two keystones the party is leaving behind. Juten Prime agrees to protect them and continue investigating the site, with Plymouth expected to verify the work later.
Juten Prime confirms that Plymouth is investigating the origins of Grixto and Galixtar.
Gerk experiments with his new Doorman portal ability, accidentally opening a portal to brackish swamp water and blasting Sylan with water before closing it.
Gerk opens another portal more carefully and reveals a hot, barren landscape filled with geysers, steam, sulfur, and brimstone.
The DM clarifies that opening or closing a gate takes an action in combat. Sylan and Gerk discuss possible tactical applications and dangers, including using environmental hazards against enemies.
Gerk and Sylan plan to practice and refine Gerk's portal ability during the journey.

Dana asks whether the site has an intact library or archive. The party learns that the former libraries and archives were largely destroyed through a combination of raiding and natural degradation, with surviving stone and written materials damaged or destroyed and only roughly the upper third of the mountain explored.
Sylan theorizes that Grixto may have learned to use the keystones through the site's archives.
The party departs by boat for Langdale Stronghold, a journey of roughly five days.
Gerk decides to practice opening doors while traveling and attempts to open a portal to his own bedroom by concentrating on the familiar location.
Gerk and Sylan determine a safer location at the rear of the ship for the experiment. Sylan uses Beacon of Hope to assist Gerk with a Wisdom saving throw, and both successfully resist losing sanity.

Gerk opens the doorway while the ship is moving, causing the rear of the ship and surrounding space to stretch dramatically toward the fixed doorway. The effect creates a powerful pull on the door and causes the ship's material to appear to stretch between the vessel and the doorway.
Gerk rolls a 31 on a Strength saving throw and maintains his grip on the doorway. He realizes that releasing it would cause him to fall because the doorway is suspended in distorted space.

Gerk calls through the doorway and asks the crew to stop and reverse the ship. The crew reverses course, causing the distortion to propagate in the opposite direction until the ship is brought back into alignment with the doorway.

Mahali sees Gerk through the doorway and pulls him into his kitchen. Gerk experiences passing through the doorway as moving through a thick, resistant barrier and explains his new Doorman ability to Mahali.

Gerk and Mahali determine that the ship's movement appears to be responsible for the dangerous stretching effect. Gerk warns that closing the doorway may trigger something significant and decides he should remain with the ship because he caused the problem.
Mahali gives Gerk and the party breakfast rolls, preserves, and butter. The party successfully passes the food tray through the doorway while the crew watches the phenomenon with concern.
Sylan recommends evacuating the stronghold in case the reality distortion affects Mahali's side of the doorway. Mahali agrees and moves the residents and guards to the tavern.

The party prepares to close the doorway using ropes and other precautions against falling. Gerk and Sylan agree to return through the door and close it, while Gerk warns that Dana may need Feather Fall.
Gerk steps back through the doorway and feels the temporal or dimensional barrier before closing it.
Closing the doorway causes reality around the ship to stretch and buckle, followed by a physical snap and a blinding light tracing the distorted path through the ship in reverse.
Gerk rolls a 5 on a d10 for the door's effect, producing a middling result on the relevant chart. The DM consults additional rules and notes to determine the unexpected consequences.
The DM determines that Gerk and Sylan are the two characters primarily affected by the magical effect because it is centered on the Doorman and his location.
Gerk and Sylan make Wisdom saving throws. Sylan succeeds with a 19, while Gerk fails and becomes confused.

A magical surge travels back toward the doorway's original position, causing reality to seemingly snap back into place. Everyone on the ship appears to disappear from the others' sight and normal communication is disrupted.

Dana and Sylan recognize the magical energy as similar to the presence of deities and discover that their spellcasting has been temporarily enhanced. Everyone with expended spell slots receives a full recovery.
A giant spectral door manifests near Gerk's former position, resembling Gerk's door or shield-like door form.
A golden, shimmering magical line remains embedded through the ship along the path of the magical discharge.

The party discovers that they cannot normally see or hear one another, although physical contact and vibrations through the ship can still cross the separation. The party realizes the phenomenon resembles their previous separation in La-rel.
Ciri tests the phenomenon by blindly striking the air and eventually makes physical contact with Sylan. Sylan confirms that he can be struck without hearing the corresponding sound.
Sylan strikes the boat and discovers that the others cannot hear the impact normally, although Ciri and Gerk can perceive the resulting vibrations.
A tray of rolls suddenly materializes and falls onto the boat. Dana and Ord take rolls, demonstrating that objects can still appear, disappear, or be interacted with despite the strange separation.
Ciri searches for her 'exit buddy' but cannot find them and continues testing whether anyone is physically nearby.
Sylan investigates the spectral door and discovers that an invisible Gerk is standing beside it. Sylan strikes Gerk in the head to confirm that someone is physically present.
Gerk remains confused and incoherent, eventually giving up on staying upright and falling to the floor. Sylan catches and supports him despite being unable to see him.
Sylan begins using gold coins to spell a message on the deck so the unseen party members can communicate and locate Gerk.
Ord considers using powder, flour, sawdust, or black powder to reveal invisible people but avoids the explosive option and instead remembers his dragon vessel.
Ord uses his dragon vessel to pour olive oil over himself. The oil creates a faint visible silhouette around him, allowing Dana and Ciri to see his general outline despite the magical invisibility.
Sylan continues interacting with the invisible Gerk while the spectral door hovers above or beside him, and uses the coins to mark Gerk's location and indicate that he is in trouble.
Gerk screams, but the others cannot hear him. Sylan turns Gerk toward the spectral door and begins dragging him toward it.
Dana uses her serpentine bracers to summon a visible large constrictor snake as a positional marker. The DM establishes that the relevant command produces two constrictor snakes.

dedupedTerms.name: Reality Distortion
notes: A phenomenon caused by opening Gerk's doorway while the ship was moving.
The ship and surrounding material stretch toward the fixed doorway like a rubber band rather than simply breaking or stopping.
Stopping and reversing the ship caused the stretching effect to reverse and ripple through the vessel.
Objects and people can pass through the distorted doorway while the ship continues moving.
Closing the doorway produced a blinding magical discharge whose final consequences were resolved through a d10/chart system.
openQuestions: What causes the reality-stretching effect?
What happens to the stretched reality when the doorway closes?

dedupedTerms.name: Spectral Door
notes: A giant, shining spectral door that appeared near or above Gerk after the magical door event.
It is closed, has no visible contents, and strongly resembles Gerk's door-shaped shield form.
Sylan determined that Gerk was physically beside the door rather than being contained within it.
Its purpose, origin, and relationship to Gerk's condition remain unknown.
openQuestions: What is the spectral door and why did it appear?
What is its relationship to Gerk's door-shaped shield and Doorman ability?
Where, if anywhere, does it lead?

dedupedTerms.name: Golden Magical Track
notes: A thin, golden, semi-fluorescent line embedded through the ship after the magical discharge.
It resembles a lightning track but leaves no burnt or damaged crevice.
openQuestions: What is the golden line and what does it signify?

dedupedTerms.name: Confusion Effect
notes: A confusion-like magical effect that struck Gerk after he failed a Wisdom saving throw during the door incident.
It left Gerk incoherent and unable to move or take meaningful actions normally.

dedupedTerms.name: Deity-like Magical Surge
notes: Magical energy experienced by Dana and Sylan during the door incident that felt similar to being in the presence of deities.
The surge temporarily enhanced their spellcasting and restored expended spell slots.
openQuestions: How exactly does the surge enhance spellcasting?

dedupedTerms.name: La-rel
notes: A realm associated with a previous incident in which party members were present but unable to see one another.
Dana and others compare the current separation phenomenon to that earlier La-rel experience.

dedupedTerms.name: Dragon Vessel
notes: An item possessed by Ord that can be used to pour liquids such as olive oil.
Ord used it to coat himself in olive oil while investigating the invisibility phenomenon, producing a faint visible outline of his body.
openQuestions: What are the full properties and intended uses of Ord's dragon vessel?

dedupedTerms.name: Serpentine Bracers
notes: Dana's bracers can summon two constrictor snakes.
The summoned snakes remain visible during the unusual invisibility phenomenon.
openQuestions: What are the complete mechanics and limitations of the serpentine bracers?

dedupedTerms.name: Constrictor Snake
notes: A large summoned snake produced by Dana's serpentine bracers.
Dana commands a summoned snake to remain at her heel as a visible positional marker.

dedupedTerms.name: Ord
notes: Dragonborn paladin and holder of the Feldspar keystone.
During the invisibility phenomenon, Ord experimented with physical substances to make affected people visible.
He used olive oil from his dragon vessel to produce a faint visible silhouette of his otherwise invisible body.
The oil silhouette demonstrated that invisible people remain physically present and can be outlined by substances.
personality: Practical and experimental, willing to improvise with unusual methods and equipment to solve problems.
openQuestions: Who or what can perceive Ord while he is invisible?

dedupedTerms.name: Ciri
notes: Half-elf rogue.
After the magical event, Ciri could not see the other party members and searched for her 'exit buddy.'
She tested whether unseen people remained physically present and eventually made physical contact with Sylan.
The phenomenon prevents normal visual perception but does not necessarily prevent physical contact.
openQuestions: Who or what is Ciri's 'exit buddy,' and why can she not find them?

dedupedTerms.name: National Flying League
notes: A flying sport or league in The Reach, jokingly compared to Quidditch.
Its season is beginning during the fall described by Walker.

dedupedTerms.name: Sunder Chase
notes: A seasonal event associated with summer rather than the current fall season.
